item.title: Briefing — Wednesday 19 August 2026
item.description: Weather. Ruislip, sixteen to twenty-four, and the forecast has the nerve to call it clear sky while also promising four millimetres of rain. Pick one. Warm, muggy, and at some point it opens on you while the app swears the sun is out. Take the jacket you will resent carrying.…

item.description: Weather. Thirty-two degrees today in Ruislip. Not a cloud, not a drop of rain, and a low of eighteen overnight, so no relief in the dark either. Linen, water, and stop pretending the fan is doing anything. And it gets worse, because Thursday is thirty-five. Thirty-five. In west…

item.title: Briefing — Tuesday 18 August 2026
item.description:
DAILY BRIEFING. Tuesday 18 August 2026.
Weather.
Ruislip today, nineteen to twenty-four, cloudy, four millimetres of rain. Grey and damp: the weather equivalent of a lukewarm cup of tea somebody forgot about. Not hot enough to enjoy, not cold enough to properly complain about,…

item.title: Briefing — Tuesday 11 August 2026
item.description: Good morning. Let's start with the weather, because Ruislip has decided this week that summer isn't asking permission anymore. Today, Tuesday, we're at seventeen to twenty-six Celsius, fair, dry as a bone, essentially zero rain, breeze barely bothering to show up at four metres…

item.title: Briefing — Thursday 20 August 2026
item.description: Weather first. Ruislip today, fourteen to twenty-one degrees and eight and a half millimetres of rain, which the forecast files under "fair". Fair! It is chucking it down and they called it fair. Twenty-one with a soaking is the worst weather there is, too warm for a coat, too…

item.title: Briefing — Thursday 13 August 2026
item.description: Weather. Thirty-five degrees. In Ruislip. Not a cloud, not a drop of rain, just the sun parked overhead like it lent you money and has come to collect. Overnight low of twenty, which is not a low, that is a warm bath. Amber heat warning in force, nurses fainting on wards, so no,…

item.description: Weather. Ruislip today, eighteen to twenty-five degrees, cloudy, nine millimetres of rain. Nine. That is not a shower, that is the sky emptying its bins on you, and still twenty-five degrees, so you get soaked and sweaty on the same trip to the car. Take the coat you will resent…

item.title: Briefing — Saturday 22 August 2026
item.description: Weather. Ruislip today. Eleven this morning, twenty-one this afternoon, fair, zero rain, wind that couldn't move a crisp packet. Eleven to twenty-one is the worst kind of day, because you dress for eleven, you commit, and by two you're carrying a coat around like a punishment.…

item.description: Weather. Ruislip. Nineteen overnight, twenty-seven this afternoon, partly cloudy, not one drop of rain, barely a breath of wind. Twenty-seven and dry on a Saturday. That is a perfect day handed to you on a plate, so get outside, and do not, under any circumstances, put on the…

item.description: Right, before anything else - before any of the news, before I even bother with good morning - let's deal with the weather, because this week is genuinely unhinged. Today in Ruislip: fifteen to twenty-seven degrees, partly cloudy, and about a tenth of a millimetre of rain, which…

item.description: Weather. Ruislip today, seventeen to twenty-five, partly cloudy, not a single drop of rain. After the summer we have had that is basically a public holiday. Go outside. Because tomorrow the sky opens and does not shut again all week. Circle Wednesday: sixteen to twenty-three and…

item.title: Briefing — Monday 10 August 2026
item.description: Right, wakey wakey. Before any news, let's deal with the weather, because Ruislip has apparently decided to have main character energy this week. Today: eighteen to twenty-six degrees, partly cloudy, not a drop of rain — mild enough, don't overthink it. Tomorrow, Tuesday:…

item.title: Briefing — Friday 21 August 2026
item.description: Weather. Ruislip. Twelve to twenty today, and the forecast has the nerve to call it clear sky while also promising two and a half millimetres of rain. Clear sky. With rain in it. Someone at the weather office is having a laugh. Twenty degrees is the most boring number ever…
